mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in three of the last four weeks and hit a new four-week low at t-0w (-11.6). Absent a reversing shock, this momentum persists via habit formation and reduced discretionary shopping trips, keeping mean RETAIL_REC lower over the next 28 days than the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined from -8.1 to -11.6 over four weeks with only one weak intermediate rebound
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the last 28 days despite no intervening rebound in TRANSIT or WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility collapsed from -10.7 to -30.4 in a single week, a magnitude consistent with a new outdoor-gathering restriction or stay-at-home order being imposed. Such policy tightening typically precedes or coincides with retail closures or capacity limits, pulling RETAIL_REC further down over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped 19.7 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises in the two weeks following a PARKS drop greater than 15 points, indicating the PARKS shock was weather- or event-driven rather than policy-driven.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has steadily recovered (-30.1 to -11.9) while TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed near -35. This divergence implies workers are shifting to private vehicles or working near home rather than resuming full commuting circuits, meaning retail foot traffic tied to transit-linked commercial precincts stays depressed even as workplace attendance partially recovers.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved ~18 points while TRANSIT changed less than 4 points over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in step with WORKPLACES recovery even while TRANSIT remains flat or declining, showing transit decoupling does not suppress retail.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stayed persistently elevated (6.0 to 5.3, never dipping below +3.6) across all four weeks, indicating sustained stay-at-home behavior characteristic of an active lockdown regime. As long as RESIDENTIAL remains above +3 points, discretionary retail trips remain suppressed, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +3 points for all four observed weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL ranged between 3.6 and 6.4 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays above +3 points, indicating the stay-at-home proxy no longer predicts retail suppression.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS decline alongside persistently negative but non-collapsing GROCERY_PHARM suggests a seasonal shift toward colder weather, driving outdoor activity indoors. This substitution effect redirects some outdoor leisure spending into indoor retail and recreation venues, nudging RETAIL_REC modestly upward over the next four weeks relative to the outdoor-heavy prior month.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell sharply while GROCERY_PHARM stayed stable near +2 to +4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline alongside falling PARKS, showing no indoor substitution effect and indicating the PARKS drop is policy-driven rather than seasonal.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has remained below -32 for all four weeks and dipped to -37.0 at t-2w, signaling a structural collapse in commuting-linked trips. When TRANSIT crosses below -35 points, co-located retail precincts near transit hubs lose footfall within one week, pulling RETAIL_REC down in the immediate short term.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -35 points in the latest week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -34.6 at t-0w and -37.0 at t-2w, both near or below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week immediately following a TRANSIT reading below -35, indicating no short-horizon transit-retail linkage.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous recovery of WORKPLACES (from -30.1 to -11.9) and the recent softening of RESIDENTIAL (6.4 down to 5.3) together indicate an easing of restrictions. When both signals move in a reopening direction at once, consumer confidence and mobility typically broaden into retail spaces within four weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC despite the current PARKS and TRANSIT weakness.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for three consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL declines for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved every week from t-3w to t-0w while RESIDENTIAL fell from 6.4 to 5.3 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next four weeks despite concurrent WORKPLACES recovery and RESIDENTIAL softening, rejecting the joint reopening signal.

mechanism_narrative: The steep week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility reflects reduced outdoor recreational outings; because retail and recreation trips in this catalog are often bundled with park visits (e.g., shopping-plus-park outings), a sharp PARKS decline directly removes a complementary trip chain, dragging RETAIL_REC down within one to two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -10.7 to -30.4 in the most recent week, the largest single-week drop in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat in the week following a sharp PARKS decline, showing no complementary trip-chain effect between parks and retail visits.
